chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding sailing the sea for trade, the man is deceived in his religion.

key_terms.يُغَرِّرُ: Is deceived / is entrapped / is led astray

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sailing the sea for trade in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns that maritime trade for commerce often leads to *gharrar* (deception or entrapment) in one's faith, a concept rooted in the historical context of long, perilous sea voyages where merchants frequently neglected prayers or engaged in doubtful transactions. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving religious integrity amidst the economic pressures and uncertainties of travel, distinguishing between necessary travel and trade pursued primarily for profit at the cost of spiritual diligence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
having said regarding sailing the sea for the business: ‘The man is deceived in his Religion’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
In sailing on the sea for trade one is deceived in his religion.’”
